## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭhamapīṭhavimānavatthu* ("Throne Mansion", Vv 1) is the opening text of the *Vimānavatthu* in the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. In this text, the arahant Moggallāna questions a *deva* regarding the past meritorious deeds that resulted in the attainment of their splendid celestial mansion [SuttaCentral]. Dhammapāla's commentary on the text explains that even very modest gifts—such as a handful of rice-beans, a rag, a spread of grass or leaves, or a gall-nut in decomposing cattle-urine—bestowed with a devout heart upon a worthy recipient yield great karmic fruit and splendor, illustrating the karmic efficacy of selfless generosity [Neelis 2011]. Six translations of the text in six languages are indexed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language parallels or early external alignments are documented for this text [DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus demonstrates extensive Pali-internal formulaic reuse across 27 texts (167 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Outside of its extensive commentary in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the text shares substantial passage material with subsequent "chair/throne" stories, specifically the *Dutiyapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 2, where segments §0.1–9.1 align with §0.1–8.1), *Tatiyapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 3), and *Catutthapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 4), as well as other *Vimānavatthu* narratives including the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Dīpavimānavatthu* (Vv 9), *Tatiyanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 8), and the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
